name: Insulin degludec
route_note: subcutaneous injection once daily at any time of day (100 or 200 U/mL)

discovery.note: B30 threonine removed and a hexadecanedioic acid side chain attached to B29 lysine via a glutamic acid linker.

tagline: Basal insulin that forms multi-hexamer chains under the skin, lasting over 42 hours
summary: Insulin degludec is an ultra-long-acting basal insulin with a half-life of about 25 hours and a duration of action beyond 42 hours. Its flat, stable profile allows flexible once-daily dosing, and the DEVOTE trial showed less severe hypoglycaemia than insulin glargine with similar cardiovascular safety.
mechanism: Degludec lacks threonine B30 and carries a 16-carbon fatty diacid on lysine B29. In the pen it exists as dihexamers with phenol and zinc; after injection phenol diffuses away and the dihexamers link into long soluble multi-hexamer chains that slowly release monomers.
The fatty-acid side chain also binds albumin in the circulation, further prolonging action. Released insulin acts on the insulin receptor to lower blood glucose in the same way as human insulin.
uses: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (adults and children aged 1 year and over)
Type 2 diabetes mellitus requiring basal insulin

history.title: First approval
history.detail: Tresiba is approved in Japan in September 2012.

history.title: EU approval; FDA delay
history.detail: The European Commission approves Tresiba in January 2013; FDA issues a complete response letter requesting cardiovascular outcomes data.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: After interim cardiovascular data, FDA approves Tresiba and Ryzodeg in September 2015.

history.title: Xultophy
history.detail: Fixed combination with liraglutide (Xultophy 100/3.6) is approved by FDA.

history.title: DEVOTE results
history.detail: The DEVOTE trial shows non-inferior cardiovascular safety and lower rates of severe hypoglycaemia versus glargine U100.

pk.half_life: about 25 h; duration of action >42 h; steady state after 2–3 days
pk.bioavailability: not fully characterised; slow SC absorption

facts: Degludec's US approval was delayed two years until a cardiovascular outcomes analysis was provided.
The DEVOTE trial randomised about 7,600 people with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk.

references.title: Marso SP et al. DEVOTE: degludec vs glargine cardiovascular safety (NEJM 2017)
